articles.title: AI SPEND IS MOVING FASTER THAN TEAMS CAN TRACK
articles.summary:
An unattended AI agent can burn through a week of tokens without warning. And when no one has a complete view of AI usage, everyone gets surprised by the bill. That's why it's important for IT, Finance, and AI program leaders to work from shared data before the invoice arrives.

THIS GUIDE [5] to AI spend management covers:

* Why AI spend varies by consumption, model, and use cases * What IT, Finance, and AI program leaders each need to see and manage AI consumption and spend * How centralized data can help leaders to proactively manage spend

articles.title: ACCENTURE WEIGHS $1.5 BILLION SALE OF ITS CHINA CONSULTING BUSINESS
articles.summary: Accenture has hired JPMorgan to explore the sale of its Greater China consulting operations in a deal potentially worth up to $1.5 billion. The strategic review follows unsolicited interest and comes as Beijing restricts foreign consultants from advising state-owned enterprises. Meanwhile, Accenture is redirecting capital and focus toward expanding its artificial intelligence capabilities globally.

articles.title: OPENAI REPORTS MAJOR GAINS IN LEGACY-CODE MODERNIZATION
articles.summary: OpenAI introduced evaluations for building software across 20 programming languages and migrating COBOL while preserving behavior. On its COBOL migration benchmark, GPT-6.1 Sol reached 86.6% accuracy at low reasoning effort, compared with 5.4% for GPT-5.6 Sol, suggesting progress on maintaining and modernizing legacy enterprise systems.

articles.title: MICROSOFT EXITS UK DATA CENTER DEAL AMID POWER DELAYS
articles.summary: Microsoft reportedly terminated its agreement for capacity at Nscale's planned Loughton facility amid electricity supply delays that could extend into the 2030s. Nscale says the development will proceed and its other Microsoft contracts remain unaffected, highlighting the growing importance of power availability in AI infrastructure planning.

articles.title: ENTERPRISE AI OUTCOMES DEPEND ON THE ART OF UNLEARNING
articles.summary: Enterprise AI adoption often falls short because organizations overlook the human element of change management. Successful digital transformation in the agentic era requires empowering employees to unlearn old software habits, supported by dedicated roles like Forward Deployed Engineers and Agentic Design Leads.

articles.title: THE AGENTS NOBODY MEANT TO BUILD
articles.summary: IT leaders face an emerging challenge with unsanctioned AI agents created inadvertently by employees using approved desktop tools and recurring workflows. Gartner forecasts that 40% of enterprises will demote or shut down agents by 2027 due to governance gaps, security risks, and a lack of ownership visibility. Managing this risk requires placing hard limits on what agents can touch and integrating education directly into tool access.

articles.title: ENTERPRISE AI NEEDS RUNTIME GOVERNANCE AND BETTER CONTEXT
articles.summary: Scaling enterprise AI requires coordinating what agents know with what they are permitted to do. Runtime access controls, audit trails, retrieval, and memory need to work together as agents operate across enterprise systems.

articles.title: LENOVO'S AI EXPRESS TARGETS ENTERPRISES WAITING FOR AI SERVERS
articles.summary: Lenovo's AI Express is a quick-ship programme developed with Nvidia that aims to cut enterprise AI server lead times to as little as 15 business days. The offering provides three pre-validated configurations ranging from small inference setups to large generative AI platforms using Blackwell hardware. The program is designed for enterprises struggling with hardware scarcity. Orders are subject to strict caps and eligibility checks.

articles.title: CLOUDFLARE EXPANDS ENTERPRISE INTEGRATIONS FOR ITS AI WORKSPACE
articles.summary: Cloudflare expanded the partner ecosystem for Cloudflare OS with integrations spanning Asana, Box, Canva, ClickHouse, GitHub, Gong, and Notion. The announcement also adds professional services partners to help enterprises train employees and adopt AI workflows connected to their existing tools.

articles.title: CISCO SECURE EMAIL GATEWAY ZERO-DAY EXPLOITED AGAIN
articles.summary: Cisco confirmed that a zero-day vulnerability in its Secure Email Gateway, tracked as CVE-2026-76519 with a CVSS score of 9.8, is actively being exploited in the wild. The path traversal flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to write files and execute root-level commands via crafted email attachments when File Reputation is enabled. Security agencies, including CISA and Germany's BSI, have issued warnings and urgent patching deadlines.

articles.title: WHY GPU CLOUD OBSERVABILITY IS HARDER THAN IT LOOKS
articles.summary: GPU cloud observability requires connecting physical infrastructure topology with active workloads, yet traditional monitoring tools often remain isolated by subsystem. Building a live, topology-aware model enables operators to trace performance bottlenecks, manage capacity fragmentation, and correlate hardware telemetry with distributed training or inference jobs.

articles.title: IBM DOESN'T NEED TO SELL MORE PRODUCTS, IT NEEDS TO SELL ITS ENTERPRISE AI HARNESS
articles.summary: IBM successfully scaled an internal AI harness built over two and a half years to a significant portion of its client base, demonstrating a viable business model for enterprise transformation.

articles.title: OPENCODE REPORTS ACCOUNT COMPROMISE
articles.summary: Attackers compromised an older OpenCode system, affecting 1.4% of Console users.
